title: FDA Seizes 9.4 Tonnes of Paneer and Khoya Worth Rs 28.4 Lakh in Pune
excerpt: The Maharashtra FDA seized 9,000 kg of paneer and 440 kg of khoya at Bavdhan, Kasba Peth and Bibwewadi on October 19, finding consignments from Karnataka transported and stored without proper temperature control, days before Diwali.
body:
• Maharashtra's Food and Drug Administration seized 9,440 kg of paneer and khoya worth Rs 28.40 lakh in Pune on Monday, October 19, at Bavdhan, Kasba Peth and Bibwewadi.
  • The stock — 9,000 kg of paneer and 440 kg of khoya brought in from Karnataka — was found being transported and stored without proper temperature control, the FDA's preliminary report said.
  • The break-up was 3,200 kg of paneer in Bavdhan, 3,040 kg of paneer plus the 440 kg of khoya in Kasba Peth, and 2,760 kg of paneer in Bibwewadi; legal action is proceeding under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, with testing still to establish quality and safety.
  • Consumer check: before buying paneer or khoya for Diwali sweets, look for a printed manufacturing date and FSSAI licence number and buy only from refrigerated stock — and report suspect stock through the FSSAI consumer grievance portal linked in this article.

The Food and Drug Administration seized 9,440 kg of paneer and khoya valued at Rs 28.40 lakh during inspections at Bavdhan, Kasba Peth and Bibwewadi in Pune on Monday, October 19, after finding the perishable dairy products were being transported and stored without proper temperature control, according to DCN News Network, reporting the FDA's preliminary action report.

The operation began at 6 am and covered consignments brought to Pune from Karnataka. The seized stock comprised 9,000 kg of paneer and 440 kg of khoya. Officials suspect the products may be unsafe for consumption, though quality and safety will have to be established through further examination, DCN reported.

Where the Stock Was Seized

In Bavdhan, officials seized 3,200 kg of paneer worth Rs 9.60 lakh. In Kasba Peth, they confiscated another 3,040 kg of paneer valued at Rs 9.12 lakh, along with 440 kg of khoya worth Rs 1.40 lakh. The remaining 2,760 kg of paneer, valued at Rs 8.28 lakh, was seized in Bibwewadi.

The khoya consignment was linked to Shivshankar Dairy near Dengle Bridge in Kasba Peth and was being transported in a vehicle registered KA 23 B 7149. Two other vehicles, registered KA 71 2453 and KA 71 0406, were identified in connection with the paneer consignments, according to the preliminary report cited by DCN.

The same Pune quantities — 9,000 kg of paneer and 440 kg of khoya — were also listed for the Pune division in statewide Maharashtra FDA crackdown reporting by Daily Kiran on October 21, which put total seizures across the state at about Rs 3.11 crore.

Why Temperature Control Matters

The FDA's preliminary findings were that the dairy products were being handled and sold in the open under uncontrolled temperature conditions. Paneer and khoya are highly perishable and require appropriate storage and transport to maintain quality. Exposure to unsuitable temperatures can accelerate spoilage and create conditions favourable for microbial growth, potentially increasing the risk of foodborne illness, DCN reported.

DCN also noted that another account of the operation reported the products lacked printed manufacturing dates and food safety information. The FDA's preliminary report did not establish whether the seized stock was adulterated, counterfeit or otherwise unsafe. Further testing is expected to determine whether the products meet food safety standards, and the department is proceeding with legal action under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. Laboratory results and any further action against the suppliers were not available in the preliminary report.

Diwali-Season Context

The seizure came just days before Diwali, when demand for paneer-based dishes, sweets and other dairy products typically increases, DCN reported. Khoya is a base ingredient for many festival sweets, and paneer demand rises in homes and restaurants through the season, which is why consignments transported over long distances, in this case from Karnataka, draw inspection attention at entry points and markets.

What Consumers Can Check and Report

The practical checks are on the pack and the shelf: buy paneer and khoya only where they are kept refrigerated, look for a printed manufacturing date, best-before date and FSSAI licence number, and avoid stock displayed in the open without cold storage — the exact failure found in this seizure. Consumers can lodge a food-safety grievance through the FSSAI consumer grievance portal, or through the Maharashtra FDA's grievance route, with the seller's name and location and a photo of the product and label where available. For diaspora families ordering festival sweets for relatives in Pune, the same check applies at the sweet shop: ask whether the khoya and paneer stock is refrigerated and labelled before placing a large Diwali order.
